ai.description: *Hemidactylus treutleri* reaches 60–70 mm SVL. It is pale grey-brown with dark dorsal spots and a white underside. Key features include strongly keeled dorsal tubercles and a distinct, unsegmented tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus treutleri* is best distinguished by its lack of enlarged, keeled tubercles on the back, which are instead replaced by small, uniform, granular scales.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus treutleri* inhabits dry deciduous forests and rocky outcrops within the Indian subcontinent, typically found at elevations ranging from 300 to 900 meters.
ai.behavior: *Hemidactylus treutleri* is a nocturnal gecko that actively hunts insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks, utilizing its adhesive toe pads to navigate vertical terrain.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus treutleri* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity during the monsoon season in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus treutleri* is endemic to the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, typically found at elevations ranging from 100 to 1,100 meters.
